subtopics.title: The Normal Force and the Free-Body Diagram

questions.question: The normal force is best described as:
options: The force a surface exerts on an object, perpendicular to the surface
The ordinary force of gravity on an object
A force that always equals the object's weight
The friction between two smooth surfaces

questions.question: A 40 kg box is pulled by a rope with 80 N at 25° ABOVE the horizontal. The normal force is:
If the same 80 N rope instead pushes at 25° BELOW the horizontal, the normal force becomes:
Getting the normal force wrong is expensive mainly because:
options: The weight must then be recalculated
The free-body diagram must be redrawn
The mass changes with the normal force
Friction is calculated from N, so every later friction value inherits the error

questions.question: A 60 kg crate (μs = 0,5) stands on a level floor. Its maximum static friction is:
That crate is pushed horizontally with 250 N and does not move. The friction acting on it is:
Pushed with 320 N, the crate slides (μk = 0,35). Its acceleration is:
Which statement about the coefficients of friction is TRUE?
options: μk exceeds μs for all surface pairs
The coefficients are measured in newtons
The coefficients grow with contact area
μs exceeds μk, they carry no unit, and contact area is irrelevant

subtopics.title: Resolving Weight on an Inclined Plane

questions.question: On an inclined plane the most convenient axes are:
options: Parallel and perpendicular to the slope
Along the weight and along the friction

questions.question: The component of the weight PARALLEL to a slope at angle θ is:
On a frictionless or rough slope alike, the normal force equals:
options: mg cosθ, which is always less than the weight

questions.question: As a slope gets steeper, the normal force:
options: Decreases, so the available grip decreases too

subtopics.title: Worked Incline Problems — Sliding, Held and Pushed

questions.question: A 15 kg toolbox rests on a 35° ramp. The component of its weight along the slope is:
With μs = 0,6, the maximum static friction on that ramp (N = 120,4 N) is 72,2 N. The toolbox:
options: Stays put, since friction can always match gravity
Slides, because the 84,3 N downhill pull exceeds the 72,2 N grip ceiling
Stays put, because 72,2 N exceeds 84,3 N
Cannot be analysed without its speed

questions.question: Once sliding (μk = 0,25), the toolbox's acceleration down the ramp is:
Dragging the toolbox UP the ramp at constant velocity requires a force of 114,4 N because:
options: The normal force doubles during upward motion
Static friction must first be broken again
Gravity increases on a moving object
Kinetic friction now acts DOWN the slope, joining the 84,3 N weight component: 84,3 + 30,1

subtopics.title: Grip, and Why It Runs Out

questions.question: You shove a wardrobe with 200 N and it does not move. Static friction is currently:
The wardrobe feels easier to push once it is already sliding because:
options: Kinetic friction is weaker than maximum static friction
The normal force disappears during motion

questions.question: Friction is calculated by multiplying:
options: The weight by the applied force
The coefficient μ by the normal force
The coefficient μ by the mass

subtopics.title: Gravity Split into Down-the-Slope and Into-the-Slope

questions.question: On a ramp, gravity's single downward pull is shared between:
options: A downhill share along the slope and a pressing share into the slope
A forward share and a backward share
The two ends of the ramp

questions.question: A 147 N toolbox sits on a 35° ramp. The surface pushes back with:
options: 120,4 N — the pressing share, smaller than the weight

questions.question: Grip weakens on steeper slopes because:
options: The coefficient of friction shrinks with angle
More of the weight pulls downhill and less presses into the surface, so N and the friction built on it both shrink
The surface becomes smoother when tilted

questions.question: The downhill share of the weight on a slope of angle θ is:

subtopics.title: Will It Slide? The Quick Test

questions.question: The quick slide test compares:
options: The downhill share of gravity against the grip ceiling μs × N
The weight against the normal force
The applied force against the weight

questions.question: When the toolbox is dragged UP the ramp, friction acts:
options: Up the slope, helping the mechanic
Down the slope, opposing the uphill motion

questions.question: The mass-free slipping test says an object on a slope slides when:
options: The sine of the angle exceeds the mass
tanθ exceeds the coefficient of static friction
The weight exceeds the normal force

questions.question: For the 35° ramp with μs = 0,6, the test gives tan35° = 0,700. Therefore:
options: Any toolbox slides, regardless of its mass, since 0,700 exceeds 0,6
Nothing slides, since 0,6 is less than 0,700
